newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end weak, leaders hit by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end weak, leaders hit by profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking in Hong Kong's leading stocks brought the Hang Seng Index to a lower close on Thursday, but lagging counters received a boost as investors sought out bargains, brokers said.
The blue chip index ended 23.52 points, or 0.17 percent, lower at 14,212.00. Turnover was HK$14.21 billion compared with HK$16.15 billion on Wednesday.
"All the ones that have led the market are being hit," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities. "There is resistance around these levels."

Property developers led Thursday's decline, with shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd down HK$1.50 at HK$77.00, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd off HK$0.75 at HK$93.75 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd down HK$0.75 to HK$74.50.
"The big developers are running out of steam but there is a big catch up from the property investors," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.

He said there had been some "healthy rotational buying" into laggard stocks like in Wharf (Holdings) Ltd, which jumped HK$1.30 to HK$33.30, and Swire Pacific Ltd, which added HK$1.75 during the session before finishing unchanged at HK$64.00.
"I think people will be switching out of the fully-valued stocks and into things like Wharf," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
Remington said crackdown measures on Chinese stocks had also dampened sentiment. Beijing said on Wednesday it would ban state enterprises and listed firms from speculative stock trading.
The Shanghai B share index tumbled 6.34 percent to close at 82.583 points and the Shenzhen B share index dropped 8.29 percent to 150.86 points.
"I think this probably will filter through to Hong Kong," said Remington.
Red chip Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd fell HK$1.10 to HK$43.10. The H-share index fell 4.65 points to 1,061.04.
Osborn said some concerns about the huge demand generated by Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd's initial public offering had also rekindled fears that China would step in cool down red chips.
"Previous attempts to cool down the red chips have not worked. There is some concern that China should actually get tougher," he said.
Renewed speculation about Hongkong Telecom's shareholding structure boosted the stock HK$0.367 to HK$16.00.
The stock went ex-dividend on Thursday.
